evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/workflow-automation/pages/AutomationRulesPage.tsx:56-72 — the three destructive/side-effecting mutations are awaited with no try/catch and no onError: confirmDelete() does `await deleteRule.mutateAsync(deleteConfirm.id); setDeleteConfirm(null);` (56-61); handleToggle() does `await updateRule.mutateAsync({id, data:{isEnabled}})` (63-68); handleRun() does `await runRule.mutateAsync(rule.id)` (70-72). None of the three mutation hooks (useUpdateAutomationRule / useDeleteAutomationRule / useRunAutomationRule, lines 44-46) is passed an onError, and no mutation isError branch is rendered. Only the *query* error is surfaced (lines 178-182).

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/main.tsx:28-35 — the app QueryClient sets only `defaultOptions.queries` (staleTime, retry); there is NO MutationCache and NO `defaultOptions.mutations.onError`. Grep confirms no MutationCache/onError in src/lib or main.tsx. So a failed delete/toggle/run is surfaced nowhere: the user sees no error toast/banner, and because these use `mutateAsync` without a catch, a rejected mutation becomes an unhandled promise rejection. For confirmDelete specifically, a rejection also skips `setDeleteConfirm(null)`, leaving the confirmation modal stuck open with no feedback. Landable frontend-only remedy: wrap each mutateAsync in try/catch with a user-facing error (toast or inline banner), or add a global MutationCache onError to the QueryClient in main.tsx.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/workflow-automation/pages/AutomationRulesPage.tsx — page-level user-facing copy is hardcoded English with no t() wrapping: 'Automation Rules' / 'Create and manage automated workflows...' (82-85), 'Create Rule' (101), filter option labels 'All Status'/'Active'/'Paused' (150-152) and 'All Triggers'/'Time Based'/... (167-171), 'Failed to load automation rules. Please try again.' (180), 'No automation rules yet' + body (217-219), 'Create Your First Rule' (240), 'Showing N of M rules' (246), and the whole delete-confirm modal ('Delete Automation Rule', 'This action cannot be undone.', 'Are you sure...', 'Cancel', 'Deleting...'/'Delete') (285-306).

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/workflow-automation/pages/CreateRulePage.tsx:50-64 — 'Back to Rules', 'Create Automation Rule', 'Set up a new automated workflow...', and the error string 'Failed to create automation rule. Please try again.' are all hardcoded. These page files do not import useTranslation (grep shows t()/useTranslation only in this feature's *components* like RuleBuilder/TemplatePreviewModal, not its pages). This is an i18n gap against the app norm: 261 of 445 non-test feature TSX files use react-i18next. Landable frontend-only remedy: add useTranslation to the workflow-automation pages and move the strings into the i18n catalog.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/workflow-automation/pages/CreateRulePage.tsx:18-20 — handleSave receives `rule: Partial<AutomationRule>` from RuleBuilder and then does `await createRule.mutateAsync(rule as AutomationRule)`, an unchecked widening cast across the API/mutation boundary. If RuleBuilder emits a rule missing required AutomationRule fields (e.g. an unfinished step), TypeScript is silenced by the cast and the incomplete object is sent to the create endpoint, converting a compile-time guarantee into a runtime 400/500. The Frontend checklist flags `as`-casts that cross an API boundary. Landable frontend-only remedy: have RuleBuilder's onSave produce a validated full AutomationRule (or a dedicated CreateAutomationRule request type) so the cast is unnecessary, or validate required fields before mutateAsync.
